title: Concurrency & workers
lede: Real OS threads with cross-thread messaging: Node's worker_threads, ported from Node's own lib/internal/worker, plus the web's Worker/onmessage shape. Each Worker is an isolate — on its own thread it evaluates its modules afresh — and messages are structured clones of any value, with SharedArrayBuffer/Atomics for shared memory and MessagePorts moving between threads in a transfer list. The one structural difference: a worker's file is compiled into the program, so new Worker takes a path literal.

entries.name: Worker
entries.signature: new Worker(filename: string | URL, options?: WorkerOptions): Worker
entries.description: Spawns a real OS thread running one of the program's worker modules as an isolate: on its thread it evaluates every builtin module and the modules the file imports afresh, then the file. The Worker is Node's (an EventEmitter with 'online', 'message', 'error', 'exit', postMessage, terminate() resolving the exit code, ref/unref, threadId); the web's onmessage/onerror shape and a worker's self.onmessage/self.postMessage work too. Messages are structured clones of any value; a SharedArrayBuffer keeps its memory, and a MessagePort in the transfer list moves to the other thread. An uncaught error in the worker reaches the parent's 'error', then 'exit' with code 1.

params.name: filename
params.desc: A path literal (or __filename) naming a worker module; resolved relative to the file it is written in.

returns.desc: An EventEmitter with postMessage, terminate, ref/unref and threadId.

differences: A worker's file is compiled in: `new Worker` takes a path literal (resolved relative to the file it is written in) or `__filename`; a computed path or `eval: true` code fails at `new Worker`
`terminate()` takes effect at the worker's next event-loop turn: a worker busy in synchronous code runs on until it yields
A TypedArray view over a `SharedArrayBuffer` is copied, not shared: send the buffer and re-view it
A transferred `ArrayBuffer` is copied, not detached
A worker shares `process.env` with its parent and writes `stdout`/`stderr` directly; the stdio/env/resourceLimits/argv/execArgv options and `getHeapSnapshot()` are not ported
An `'uncaughtException'` listener in a worker runs but the worker still ends with code 1

entries.name: BroadcastChannel
entries.description: Name-keyed pub/sub across threads through a process-wide registry: each other open channel of the name gets its own structured clone of the message, delivered on its own thread's loop. An open channel holds the loop until close(), as Node's does; onmessage, addEventListener/removeEventListener and ref()/unref() work same-thread and across workers.

returns.desc: An endpoint with postMessage, onmessage, addEventListener and close.

entries.name: MessageChannel / MessagePort
entries.signature: new MessageChannel(): { port1: MessagePort, port2: MessagePort }
entries.description: An entangled port pair. A port is Node's NodeEventTarget: on('message') or onmessage starts it, addEventListener works, close() closes both ends and each emits 'close', and ref()/unref()/hasRef() control whether it holds the loop. A port moves to another thread in a postMessage transfer list or a Worker's transferList, and is detached on the sending side; one outside the transfer list is a DataCloneError. Globals, and importable from worker_threads.

entries.name: klain:sync goroutines, channels, select
entries.statusRow: klain:sync goroutines, channels, select (go, Channel<T>, select)
entries.signature: import { go, Channel, select, defaultCase } from 'klain:sync'; go(fn: () => void); new Channel<T>(capacity?); select(...cases)
entries.description: An explicitly-non-Node opt-in: Go's concurrency model, not a JS approximation. go(fn) spawns a cheap goroutine onto a GMP work-stealing scheduler (one logical processor + pinned OS thread per GOMAXPROCS, global run-queue backstop, half-queue stealing) in an embedded C runtime linked only when klain:sync is imported. Channel<T> is a Go channel: synchronous blocking send/receive (not await) that parks the goroutine — the OS thread keeps running others — as an unbuffered rendezvous or buffered ring, with close() and `for (const v of ch)` range. select(...) is Go's random-fair select over recvCase/sendCase/defaultCase. Cooperative preemption is complete: a sysmon thread flags an over-budget goroutine and compiler-inserted safepoints at every function entry and loop back-edge yield it, so no goroutine can starve the others.

params.name: fn
params.desc: go(fn): the goroutine body; captures channels from its enclosing scope.

params.name: capacity
params.desc: new Channel<T>(capacity): 0/omitted is an unbuffered rendezvous; >0 is a buffered ring.

params.name: ...cases
params.desc: select(...): ch.recvCase(handler) / ch.sendCase(value, handler) / defaultCase(handler); runs one ready case, or blocks until one fires (unless a defaultCase is present).

returns.desc: go returns nothing; new Channel<T> returns a channel with .send(v: T)/.receive(): T/.close().

differences: Channel ops are synchronous blocking, not await; the element is a fixed 8-byte slot (number/string/object/boolean).

select cases are ch.recvCase(v => ...) / ch.sendCase(x, () => ...) / defaultCase(() => ...); a recv handler gets the value but not the closed flag — use the for-of range (which ends on close) to detect it.

Fixed goroutine stacks (default 256 KiB, tunable via KLAINSYNC_STACK_KB); true growable/moving stacks are gated on precise stack maps. Blocking-syscall P-handoff is a bounded sysmon rescue-M approximation. send-after-close / double-close abort the process (Go-panic parity); native-only.
